description: Experience the rich and complex flavors of Pollo en Mole, a truly iconic Mexican dish. This traditional recipe combines tender chicken with a deeply savory, slightly sweet, and subtly spicy mole sauce, crafted from a blend of chilies, spices, nuts, and a hint of chocolate. It's a culinary journey that brings the heart of Mexico to your table with every delicious bite.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken and Chiles
instructions.text: Season chicken pieces generously with salt. In a large pot, bring 4 cups of chicken broth to a simmer. Add the chicken and cook until just tender, about 20-25 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside, reserving the broth. While chicken cooks, toast the dried chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat for 1-2 minutes per side until fragrant. Be careful not to burn them. Remove from heat, place in a bowl, and cover with hot water for 20 minutes to rehydrate. Drain well.

instructions.title: Toast Nuts, Seeds, and Spices
instructions.text: In the same dry skillet, toast almonds, peanuts, and sesame seeds separately until lightly golden and fragrant. Transfer to a plate. Next, toast the cinnamon stick, cloves, peppercorns, and cumin seeds until aromatic, about 1 minute. Add these to the plate with the nuts.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics and Other Ingredients
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in the skillet. Add chopped tomatoes, tomatillos, onion, and garlic. Sauté until softened and lightly browned, about 8-10 minutes. Add the raisins and torn tortilla or bread piece to the skillet and cook for another 2 minutes. Remove from heat.

instructions.title: Blend the Mole Paste
instructions.text: Combine the rehydrated chiles, sautéed vegetables, toasted nuts, seeds, and spices in a blender. Add about 1 cup of the reserved chicken broth. Blend until a very smooth paste forms. You may need to add more broth, a little at a time, to achieve a smooth consistency. Strain the mole paste through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl to remove any solids, pressing down with a spoon. This step is crucial for a smooth mole.

instructions.title: Simmer the Mole Sauce
instructions.text: Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Carefully add the strained mole paste to the hot oil. It will splatter, so be cautious. Cook the mole, stirring constantly, for about 10-15 minutes, allowing it to deepen in color and flavor. Add the chopped Mexican chocolate and stir until completely melted. Gradually stir in the remaining reserved chicken broth until the sauce reaches your desired consistency. Bring to a gentle simmer and season with salt to taste. Continue to simmer for at least 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, for the flavors to meld.

instructions.title: Combine Chicken with Mole
instructions.text: Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering mole sauce. Ensure the chicken is fully submerged and coated. Continue to simmer for another 10-15 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors of the mole and heat through. Serve hot, garnished with a sprinkle of sesame seeds and fresh cilantro, if desired. Pollo en Mole is traditionally served with Mexican rice and warm tortillas.

tips: For an even richer flavor, lightly fry the chicken pieces in a little oil after boiling and before adding them to the mole sauce.
If you cant find specific dried chiles, you can adjust with what's available, but the classic three (ancho, mulato, pasilla) offer the most authentic flavor profile.
Mole sauce can be made ahead of time and stored in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days, or frozen for longer. Its flavor often improves overnight.
article:
Unlock the rich, complex flavors of Mexico right in your kitchen with one of its most revered culinary masterpieces: Pollo en Mole, or Chicken Mole. This iconic dish is more than just a meal; it's a celebration of heritage, a symphony of ingredients, and a testament to the depth of Mexican cuisine. If you've ever been intimidated by the thought of making mole from scratch, fear not! This comprehensive guide will walk you through the journey of creating an authentic and incredibly delicious Chicken Mole sauce, turning your kitchen into a vibrant Mexican fiesta.

## What is Chicken Mole (Pollo en Mole)?

At its heart, Pollo en Mole translates simply to "chicken in mole sauce." But to say "mole sauce" is to open a culinary universe. Mole (pronounced MOH-lay) is a generic term for several types of sauces in Mexican cuisine, most notably from the states of Oaxaca and Puebla. These sauces are renowned for their incredibly complex flavor profiles, often involving dozens of ingredients. A traditional mole can include various chiles, spices, nuts, seeds, fruits, vegetables, and even chocolate, all ground together to form a thick, velvety sauce.

The history of mole is as rich and layered as its flavor, with origins tracing back to pre-Hispanic times. While there are many regional variations – from the fiery Mole Poblano to the sweeter Mole Negro – they all share a common thread: a labor of love that results in a sauce unlike any other. When paired with tender, succulent chicken, the dish transforms into Pollo en Mole, a comforting and deeply satisfying experience that perfectly balances savory, sweet, smoky, and spicy notes. It's a dish often reserved for special occasions, holidays, and family gatherings, embodying the warmth and generosity of Mexican culture.

## Ingredients You Need for Chicken Mole

Crafting an authentic Chicken Mole sauce requires a diverse array of ingredients, each playing a crucial role in building its signature depth. Don's be overwhelmed by the list; many are pantry staples, and the reward is truly worth the effort.

For the Chicken:
*   2-3 lbs bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces (thighs, drumsticks, breasts), or boneless chicken for quicker cooking
*   1 onion, halved
*   2-3 garlic cloves
*   Salt to taste

For the Mole Sauce:
*   Dried Chiles: 4-5 ancho chiles (for fruity, mild heat), 3-4 mulato chiles (for earthy, smoky notes), 2-3 pasilla chiles (for deep, rich flavor). For a bit of kick, add 1-2 arbol chiles.
*   Aromatics: 1/2 white onion, 3-4 garlic cloves
*   Spices: 1 tsp whole black peppercorns, 1/2 tsp whole cumin seeds, 1/4 tsp whole cloves, 1 small stick cinnamon (Mexican canela preferred), 1/4 tsp anise seeds (optional)
*   Nuts & Seeds: 1/4 cup raw almonds, 1/4 cup raw peanuts, 2 tbsp pumpkin seeds (pepitas), 1 tbsp sesame seeds
*   Bread/Tortilla: 1 slice stale bread or 1 stale corn tortilla, torn
*   Tomatoes/Tomatillos: 1 large ripe tomato or 2-3 tomatillos, roasted
*   Raisins: 1/4 cup dark raisins
*   Chocolate: 1-2 oz Mexican chocolate (e.g., Ibarra or Abuelita), or good quality dark chocolate (70% cacao or higher), chopped
*   Broth: 4-6 cups chicken broth (from cooking the chicken or store-bought)
*   Oil: 2-3 tbsp vegetable oil or lard
*   Salt and sugar to taste

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Pollo en Mole

Making Chicken Mole is a process, but each step builds towards an incredible culinary creation.

1.  **Cook the Chicken:** Place chicken pieces, halved onion, garlic, and salt in a large pot. Cover with water and bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes until chicken is cooked through and tender. Remove chicken, strain broth, and set both aside.
2.  **Prepare the Chiles:** Stem and seed the dried chiles. Heat a dry skillet over medium heat and toast chiles in batches for 30 seconds to 1 minute per side until fragrant (do not burn). Immediately transfer to a bowl, cover with hot water, and let soak for 20-30 minutes until soft.
3.  **Toast Nuts, Seeds & Spices:** In the same dry skillet, toast almonds, peanuts, pumpkin seeds, and sesame seeds separately until lightly golden and fragrant. Remove and set aside. Then, toast peppercorns, cumin, cloves, cinnamon, and anise seeds briefly until aromatic.
4.  **Sauté Aromatics & Bread:** Heat 1-2 tablespoons of oil in a large pot or Dutch oven. Sauté the 1/2 onion and garlic until softened. Add the torn bread/tortilla and raisins, sautéing until bread is lightly golden.
5.  **Blend the Sauce:** Drain the softened chiles, reserving some of the soaking liquid. In a blender, combine the chiles, sautéed onion, garlic, bread, raisins, toasted nuts, seeds, spices, roasted tomato/tomatillos, and 1-2 cups of chicken broth. Blend until completely smooth. You may need to do this in batches and add more broth or chile soaking liquid as needed to achieve a thick, pourable consistency.
6.  **Simmer the Mole:** Heat 1-2 tablespoons of fresh oil in the same large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Carefully pour the blended mole sauce into the hot oil (it will splatter). Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low. Add the Mexican chocolate and stir until melted and fully incorporated.
7.  **Cook the Chicken in Mole:** Continue to simmer the sauce for at least 45 minutes to 1.5 hours, stirring frequently to prevent sticking. The sauce will darken, thicken, and its flavors will deepen. If it becomes too thick, add more chicken broth, a little at a time, until it reaches your desired consistency. Season with salt and a pinch of sugar to balance the flavors. Once the sauce has simmered sufficiently, add the cooked chicken pieces to the pot, ensuring they are fully coated. Simmer for another 15-20 minutes to allow the chicken to absorb the rich flavors of the mole.

## Pro Tips for the Best Chicken Mole Sauce

*   **Don't Burn the Chiles:** This is crucial! Burnt chiles will make your mole bitter. Toast them just until fragrant, then remove immediately.
*   **Patience is Key:** A truly great mole sauce needs time to simmer. The longer it simmers, the more the flavors meld and deepen, transforming from a collection of ingredients into a harmonious masterpiece.
*   **Balance the Flavors:** Taste your mole frequently. Adjust salt, and don't be afraid to add a pinch of sugar if it tastes too bitter or acidic. The chocolate is there for depth, not sweetness, so a little extra sugar can balance the heat and earthiness.
*   **Smoothness Matters:** For the silkiest mole, consider straining the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve after blending. This removes any remaining bits of chile skin or nuts, resulting in a more refined texture.
*   **Quality Ingredients:** Use good quality dried chiles and authentic Mexican chocolate if possible. These make a noticeable difference in the final flavor of your Chicken Mole.

## Serving Suggestions for Pollo en Mole

Pollo en Mole is a hearty and satisfying dish on its own, but traditional accompaniments elevate the experience. Serve your rich Chicken Mole with:

*   **Warm Corn Tortillas:** Essential for scooping up every last drop of that glorious sauce.
*   **Mexican Red Rice:** A classic pairing that complements the mole perfectly.
*   **Refried Beans:** A creamy, savory side that rounds out the meal.
*   **Garnishes:** A sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds, chopped fresh cilantro, or thinly sliced red onion adds texture and a fresh finish.

For beverages, consider a refreshing agua fresca, horchata, or a crisp Mexican lager to balance the richness of the mole.

## Variations and Substitutions for Chicken Mole

While this recipe provides a solid foundation for a classic Chicken Mole, there's always room for personal touch and adaptation:

*   **Protein Alternatives:** While chicken is traditional, mole is also excellent with turkey (especially leftover holiday turkey), pork shoulder, or even beef short ribs. For a vegetarian option, try it with roasted vegetables like sweet potatoes, cauliflower, or mushrooms, or even firm tofu.
*   **Chile Intensity:** Adjust the number of arbol chiles for more or less heat. For a milder mole, omit them entirely. For a deeper, smokier flavor, you could add a chipotle chile (rehydrated, of course).
*   **Nut Profile:** Experiment with different nuts. Pecans or walnuts can be used in place of or in addition to almonds and peanuts for a slightly different richness.
*   **Shortcut Mole Paste:** If you're short on time, high-quality prepared mole pastes (found in Mexican grocery stores or international aisles) can significantly cut down on prep. While not entirely from scratch, they offer a convenient way to enjoy the flavors of Chicken Mole. Simply dilute the paste with chicken broth and simmer, then add your cooked chicken.
*   **Fruity Notes:** Some mole recipes include plantains or apples for a touch more sweetness and fruitiness. If you enjoy that profile, try adding half a roasted plantain or apple to the blender with the other ingredients.

Crafting Pollo en Mole is a culinary adventure that rewards patience with an explosion of flavor. This iconic Mexican chicken recipe, with its deep, aromatic sauce, is a testament to the country's rich gastronomic heritage. Don't be intimidated; embrace the process, savor the aromas, and enjoy the incredible satisfaction of bringing this traditional dish to your table.
